text:
Maria (CS): putting together a small 'priming worksheet' we can hand to customers during onboarding — focused checklist for cache/prefill, batching, and streaming fallbacks. dropping draft below, please add rows you think are missing.

Ben (Eng): looks great, thx. couple quick suggestions: recommended initial batch_size=8 for short-chat workloads, 4 for high-latency models; prefill concurrency 2x normal qps for first 10m to warm kv cache.

Sam (SRE): +1. Add circuit-breaker thresholds: if 5xx rate > 3% for 2m OR p90 latency > 1200ms trigger scaledown/traffic-shift. Also add an observability snippet to watch during go-live.

Maria (CS): adding an observability checklist. also adding a small customer-facing script they can run to simulate activation prefill (feel free to tweak):

Maria (CS): ```bash
# simulate 50 prefill requests to warm shared cache
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-3b", "input":"user: hello","max_tokens":16}' &
  sleep 0.2
done
wait
```

Jordan (PM): from a renewal-risk POV, we should capture: initial latency baseline, percent of requests served from cache within first 24h, error budget burn, and a qualitative CS check-in at 72h. can we add those as metrics to share in the kickoff email?

Ben (Eng): yes — suggested metric queries to include in the kickoff report: 
`rate(http_requests_total{job="redwood",code!~"5.."}[5m])` for success QPS, 
`sum by(status) (increase(cache_hits_total[1h])) / sum(increase(cache_lookups_total[1h]))` for cache hit rate, 
`histogram_quantile(0.9, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))` for p90.

Sam (SRE): add these operational actions to the worksheet:
- Preflight (day0): confirm firewall rules + KMS access, validate model pinning, run 10 warm queries, confirm logs streaming to Splunk/Datadog.
- GoLive window (day1-3): enable 1.5x burst capacity for traffic > baseline, monitor 5xx and p90, CS should do daily check-in.
- Degrade plan: if 5xx > 5% for 5m, shift to fallback-model (quantized variant) and open incident channel #release-war-room.

Maria (CS): wording for customer email snippet (short):
"We'll run a 30-60 minute priming window to warm your tenant's cache and calibrate batching. We'll share a 24h metrics snapshot and schedule a 72h check-in to review results and next steps. If we see elevated errors we'll automatically roll to fallback model and notify you."

Jordan (PM): make sure we surface cost impact: approximate token cost for a 50-request prefill at rwd-3b and note that Dedicated tenants can request reserved warm pools to avoid burst billing.

Ben (Eng): added a short table for recommended starting configs (customer-facing):
- prefill_requests: 20-100 (based on size of prompt set)
- batch_size: 4 (latency-sensitive) / 8 (throughput)
- prefill_concurrency: 1-3
- warm_pool: requested for Dedicated or >5000 qps

Maria (CS): final ask — capture a single feedback item after the 72h check-in: did prefill reduce coldstart errors? yes/no + short note. i'll add a template to the enablement doc.

cs-bot: reminder set — follow-up checklist to @Maria (CS) scheduled in 72 hours. :white_check_mark:

Maria (CS): great work team. i'll push this worksheet into the shared enablement repo and attach to the customer kickoff email. leaving this thread open for one more pass — tag me if you add anything else. :pray:
